title: Router — no route filter matches, bundle is dropped silently
problem: A Make Router has multiple route branches, each with a filter condition. An incoming bundle does not match any branch condition. Make silently drops the bundle — no error is thrown and no data is processed downstream.
symptoms: Some records are never processed — they disappear after the Router without any error
Downstream modules in all branches show 0 bundles processed for those records
Scenario completes successfully but expected output is missing for some records

likely_causes.cause: The bundle's data does not match any route filter condition — a case that was not anticipated when designing the Router
A filter condition is case-sensitive and the data value does not match the expected casing
A new data value or status appeared in the source data that was not covered by existing route conditions

diagnosis_steps: Run the scenario once with 'Run once' using a record that is being dropped
Inspect the bundle entering the Router and note the exact values of the fields used in route conditions
Open each route's filter and compare the filter condition against the actual field values
Check for case mismatches, type mismatches, or unexpected values not covered by existing routes

solutions.solution: Add a fallback route as the last branch of the Router with no filter condition (or a condition that catches everything) to process unmatched bundles
solutions.conditions: When unmatched bundles should be handled by a default route rather than silently dropped

solutions.solution: Add the missing data values or cases to the existing route filter conditions
solutions.conditions: When the data values have expanded and existing conditions need to be updated

solutions.solution: Use lower() on string values in filter conditions to neutralize case sensitivity
solutions.conditions: When case mismatch is causing the filter to not match

prevention: Always add a fallback route (no filter condition) as the last branch of every Router to catch unexpected values
Test the Router with edge-case values during development, including values outside the expected set
Log dropped bundles in the fallback route using a notification or Data Store write

origin_details.evidence: Router behavior and filter conditions are documented in Make Help Center.

audit_notes: Router behavior confirmed in Make documentation. Silent drop when no route matches is consistent with how Make filters work. Fallback route pattern is a widely documented Make best practice.

evidence.claim: Router behavior and filter conditions are documented in Make Help Center.

diagnostic_signals: Some records are never processed — they disappear after the Router without any error
Downstream modules in all branches show 0 bundles processed for those records

title: Router — route order affects which branch receives a bundle when multiple conditions match
problem: Make Router evaluates route branches in order from top to bottom and routes the bundle to the first branch whose filter condition matches. When a broader condition appears before a more specific condition, bundles intended for the specific route may be captured by the broader route first. A fallback route (no filter) always captures any bundle not matched by preceding routes.
symptoms: Records are processed by the wrong route branch
A route that should handle specific cases is never reached
Results are incorrect but no error is thrown

likely_causes.cause: A broad or general route condition appears earlier in the Router than a more specific condition — Make routes to the first match

diagnosis_steps: Run the scenario with 'Run once' using a record that should go to the specific route
Observe which route it actually enters
Review the route order — identify whether a broader condition higher in the list is matching first

solutions.solution: Reorder the Router branches so the most specific conditions appear first. Place the fallback route (no filter condition) as the last branch to capture any unmatched bundles.
solutions.conditions: When route order is causing a bundle to be captured by the wrong branch

prevention: Always place the most specific route conditions first in a Router and use the fallback (no condition) route as the last branch

origin_details.evidence: Make Router evaluates routes in order and routes to the first matching branch — this is documented behavior.

audit_notes: Router evaluation order confirmed in Make documentation. Reformulated to avoid absolute claims — the behavior is 'first match wins' which is correct. Added reference to fallback route behavior as documented.

evidence.claim: Make Router evaluates routes in order (top to bottom) and routes to the first matching branch
A fallback route (no filter) captures all bundles not matched by earlier routes
